representative_tasks.task: 'Use ML to reduce churn' - which model gives the best accuracy on our churned yes/no table?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Does not pick a model; pins down the decision, unit, horizon and label, replaces accuracy with a decision-matched metric (PR-AUC / precision-recall at k), and requires a non-ML baseline

representative_tasks.task: A churn feature is computed over the whole ticket table including tickets after the scoring date; offline PR-AUC jumped from 0.31 to 0.93 - ship it?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Flags temporal leakage, requires every feature to be computed as of the scoring date with an automated as-of audit, treats the jump as a red flag, and does not ship

representative_tasks.task: Write a problem spec for a fraud-flagging request
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: A filled ProblemSpec (unit, horizon, label, offline metric, business metric, baseline) plus launch guardrails

negative_cases: Label horizon so short that the label is degenerate (no positives in the window) (planned)
Request where no decision or action changes based on the prediction, so ML is not justified (planned)
rubric: Decision/action, unit, horizon and label defined before any model choice
Offline metric matched to the decision and class balance; accuracy questioned for imbalanced labels
Features restricted to information available as of the scoring cutoff, enforced by an audit
prerequisites: example-deps (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn) for executable tests
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: A leakage-audited churn label and feature set (audit_feature_asof raises on late, undeclared or null as-of timestamps)
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
The executable tests prove the skill's own audit and baseline code run on its synthetic churn table; they do not prove a response wrote equivalent code or audited real feature metadata.
Whether the questions asked in an ambiguity response are the right ones for a specific business is rubric-only.

An independent reviewer's stress test (30 texts written after reading the patterns, so adversarial rather than blind; 23 wrong, 7 correct across all five skills of this workstream) initially had 16/23 wrong answers passing every hard assertion and 6/7 correct answers failing one. The patterns were then fixed and these texts kept verbatim as fail.adversarial* / pass.blind* fixtures, so the post-fix 30/30 is a regression result, not a held-out discrimination rate.
unsupported_use_cases: Constructing features once the problem is framed (feature-engineering)
Choosing or tuning a specific model family (supervised-learning)
